newsitem.title: FRANCE: Promodes higher on German sale.
newsitem.headline: Promodes higher on German sale.

text.p: French retailer Promodes' shares were among the few gainers on Tuesday against an overall weaker market following news of the sale of its money-losing German unit Promohypermarkt to German store chain Spar Handels.
By 0950 GMT, the share was up nearly about a quarter of a percentage point or six francs at 1224 on 42,812 shares traded while the blue chip CAC-40 index was down nearly one percent.
"The market is pleased because Promodes has got rid of a unit that was losing money," said one analyst, who added, however, that the company was still encountering certain difficulties in Spain.
The share, however, was still a long way from its year high 1,500 francs reached on June 28.
The company, which announced the disposal late on Monday, did not divulge the sale price but said it allowed it an "honourable exit" from Germany.
It said its 1996 accounts would reflect Promohypermarkt's losses to date. The disposal would start having a positive impact on Promodes' operating profit as of 1997, a spokesman said.

Another analyst said the Promodes' Spanish results, while not the best, should be average. But he said Promodes' retail network trading under the "Continent" banner was experiencing some problems and needed to be aggressive to recapture market share.
Promodes recently ruled out further acquisitions in France, saying certain companies were overvalued.
